task.title: M5: Delta treemap shows growth/shrink as a colored slice; drop the Changes tab
task.description:
The diverging color gradient on the compare treemap is hard to read. Replace it: every file block gets a neutral fill, and a changed file shows its relative growth or shrinkage as a vertical slice along the left edge of its block whose width is the changed fraction of the block (added lines over head code for growth, removed lines over base code for shrinkage; minimum 2px when non-zero, full width for added or removed files). Growth is GitHub's diff green and shrinkage is GitHub's diff red (the additions/deletions colors from a PR review). A file with both additions and deletions in net terms shows the net sign only. Added files get a green border as well, removed files a red border and hatched fill; unchanged files stay neutral. The legend becomes two swatches (added lines, removed lines) plus the added/removed box styles. Also remove the Changes (biggest-changes table) panel entirely: the compare panel control becomes Treemap | Edges and panel=changes in the hash falls back to treemap.

Acceptance criteria:
- On a Capacitor HEAD~5 to HEAD comparison, a file that grew 60 percent shows a green slice covering about 60 percent of its width; a file that shrank shows a red slice; unchanged files have no slice.
- Added files are fully green-sliced with a green border; removed files fully red with the hatched style; tooltips still show the deltas.
- The Changes panel, its table, the row-click handoff, and the sort comparator helpers are removed (delete dead code and its test); the switcher shows only Treemap and Edges.
- Changed only toggle still works.
- Headless Chrome check on Capacitor and workbook with no console errors.
